messages:
marina: Hey — just got an email that we're switching 401k vendors next month. Does anyone have the blackout window details and whether loans/beneficiary updates are affected? I'm going on LOA mid-cycle and want to make sure nothing breaks.

eli_hr: @marina good question. We're migrating to Altius with a planned cutover on 2026-07-01. High level:
- blackout window: ~48 hours around cutover (6/30 20:00 PT -> 7/1 08:00 PT)
- outstanding loans: will transfer but you cannot initiate new loans during the transfer window
- beneficiary updates: edits to the *old* portal freeze ~72 hours before migration; you must re-confirm or refile in the new portal after cutover

mohit_payroll: Payroll note: deductions that hit the payroll on the pay date before migration will post as usual. If you're on unpaid LOA, contributions stop automatically. If you return on partial pay, contributions are pro-rated. If people expect a change in elections while on LOA, they need to file before the payroll cutoff (2 business days before paydate).

marina: Thanks — do Roth vs pre-tax elections port over automatically? I have a 60/40 split and don't want to lose the Roth portion while I'm out.

eli_hr: Elections (Roth vs pre-tax) should port. Still recommend you log into the old portal and take a screenshot of your current elections & beneficiary page just in case. If anything looks off after migration, submit a ticket with screenshots and we'll do a manual correction.

jamie_p: Quick Q on loans: if autopay was set up through vendor payroll deduction, will it keep working after the switch? @mohit_payroll

mohit_payroll: In most cases autopay will continue since payments are handled via payroll codes. However, if vendor account mappings change there could be a hiccup. We'll notify anyone with active loans 1 week before cutover with steps. If autopay fails, vendor will accept manual payments — we will help coordinate.

benefits-bot: Migration FAQ posted: https://intranet.redwood.com/benefits/vendor-migration — includes blackout times, how to export beneficiary info, and a borrow-checklist. Expected downtime: 6/30 20:00 PT -> 7/1 08:00 PT. :information_source:

marina: Is there an offline beneficiary form I can sign now (for trust stuff)? I might need notarization while on LOA.

eli_hr: Yes — there's a fillable PDF for beneficiary designation and a notarization guidance doc. Links in the FAQ. If you need paper notarization for a trust, email me directly and I can route it to benefits ops; we handle few special cases.

marina: Perfect, I'll screenshot, grab the PDF, and ping you if I need notarization. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

eli_hr: Also, small pro tip — if you're changing deferrals before a pay period while on LOA, include your expected return date in the notes so payroll can set the correct resumption. Saves a follow-up ticket. :raised_hands:
